page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 32 vCPUs. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor, does not include local storage, and lacks integrated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core score, fall into the weak category, while single-threaded gzip compression is poor. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and Geekbench multi-core score, consistently rank in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, also demonstrate average performance.

With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is positioned for general-purpose workloads that can leverage parallel processing to offset lower single-core speeds. Factual benchmark results indicate average performance for database operations, Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation. Additionally, the CPU supports AVX-512 instructions, which assist in average-tier performance for small to medium LLM inference tasks. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this instance offers a standard resource density suitable for distributed enterprise applications, web serving, and multi-threaded utility workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance featuring 32 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: single-core performance and single-threaded compression tasks are weak, falling into the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently achieve average tier results. Supported by AVX-512 instruction sets, the instance delivers average-tier throughput for Redis operations, static web serving, and medium LLM inference. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from parallel processing.
